rule.program: ts.createProgram over an in-memory CompilerHost that can read ONLY the packed file map — no disk, no node_modules, no tsconfig, no network
rule.enumeration: checker.getExportsOfModule, with checker.getAliasedSymbol applied BEFORE reading flags so a re-export is recorded with its real kind
rule.naming: the EXPORTED name (so `export {a as b}` is `b`); the alias decides the kind, never the name
rule.kinds: value | type | unknown — and BOTH value and type break on removal (semver-ts.org / Ember RFC 0730); `unknown` is an alias chain leaving the payload
rule.ordering: Unicode CODEPOINT order, never localeCompare — a locale-sensitive sort would make the name set depend on the runner's ICU locale
rule.classification: TYPED | SFC_ENTRY | NO_SURFACE | INDETERMINATE, total and with no silent default
rule.indeterminate: a declared-but-absent target, a parse error, an unresolvable `export *`, or an unknown extension — exit 3, never a pass (A2b)
rule.noSurface: a closed list of asset extensions, or a null (blocked) target — DETERMINABLY nothing, compared only against NO_SURFACE
rule.sfcEntry: .astro resolves to the synthetic {default: value}; a TypeScript parse of the frontmatter would silently answer zero
rule.wildcards: expanded against the PACKED FILE SET, greedily across "/", exactly as Node matches subpath patterns
rule.typescriptPin: a MEASURED SET — exactly one of 5.9.2, 5.9.3, 6.0.3 (decision 0030: the whole published corpus plus 9 adversarial cases extract byte-identically under all of them). A closed enumeration, never a range: `npm i typescript` installs 7.x (the native port, no ts.createProgram), and a range would readmit it. Each repo still pins EXACTLY, to a member. Membership is asserted on the RUNTIME extraction path, not only in the conformance runner, or a drifted runtime would cache wrong names under a correctly-pinned key.
rule.referenceCache: a cached surface is usable Level-2 evidence only when it carries a `names` FIELD (never: a non-empty one) — an all-asset package is legitimately empty, while a pre-Level-2 entry must never read as an empty name set

cases.why: BOTH KINDS BREAK ON REMOVAL, so both must be enumerated. A classifier that drops type-only names would make `export interface Options` deletable under a patch.
A class and an enum carry a VALUE binding as well as a type; recording them as type-only would understate what a removal costs.

files.index.d.ts:
export declare class Widget {}
export declare enum Level { Low, High }

cases.why: `default` IS part of the surface — removing it breaks `import x from "pkg"` exactly as removing a named export does.

files.index.d.ts:
declare const thing: number;
export default thing;

cases.why: RESOLVE ALIASES BEFORE READING FLAGS. Without getAliasedSymbol every re-export reads as a bare Alias — no Value bit, no Type bit — so a re-exported value would be indistinguishable from a re-exported type (pre-mortem 4).

files.inner.d.ts:
export declare const inner: number;
export interface Shape { x: number }

cases.why: A consumer imports `outer`, not `inner`. Alias resolution decides the KIND, never the name.
A resolvable `export *` contributes its names transitively; refusing to follow it would understate the surface.

files.inner.d.ts:
export declare const a: number;
export declare const b: number;

cases.why: A2b. The names behind a bare `export *` are unknowable from the tarball alone, so the subpath is INDETERMINATE — not "zero exports". The estate has ZERO of these today; this branch keeps that measured rather than assumed.

files.index.d.ts:
export * from "zod";
export declare const mine: number;

cases.why: The counterweight to the case above: `export {Foo} from "zod"` puts the name right there in the syntax. Blocking on it would make almost every real .d.ts indeterminate, so the name is recorded with kind `unknown`.

files.index.d.ts:
export { ZodType } from "zod";
export declare const mine: number;

cases.why: THE tokens@2.0.0 CASE. It declares `.` -> ./dist/tokens.d.ts and ships neither file. "I cannot read this package's surface" must never collapse into "it has none" — that is A2b in one line.
A2b. A .d.ts that does not parse has told us nothing; a zero-name answer from it would be silently wrong.
121 of the estate's 253 subpaths are assets. Scoring them "0 exports, clean" is a meaningless green over 48% of the estate; blocking them is worse.
`"./package.json": "./package.json"` is near-universal and carries no type surface.
A `types` condition resolving to a .css is a contradiction, not an asset. Reading it as NO_SURFACE would let a real type surface vanish silently.
28 subpaths are .astro. A TypeScript parse of the frontmatter returns ZERO exports while the component genuinely exports an implicit `default` — a silently wrong answer, which is worse than an error.
The synthetic {default} is a convention about a component that SHIPPED. An absent one is unreadable, not implicitly present.
`"./x": null` blocks the subpath. A real, determinable state — and TYPED -> blocked correctly majors through the rule.
The asset list is CLOSED. "Probably an asset" is exactly the inference this rule refuses.

MEASURED on @j0nathan-ll0yd/schemas, whose `"./swift/*": "./swift/*"` glob matches a .gitkeep placeholder. A leading dot is not an extension separator, so this reports "no extension" rather than an extension of ".gitkeep" — the classification is the same either way, but the REASON a human reads must not send them hunting for a .gitkeep handler.
The estate has 9 wildcard subpaths and they glob deterministically because the file set is the TARBALL's, not the filesystem's.
A pattern with no matches publishes nothing, and that is READ off the packed file set, not guessed.

MEASURED AGAINST NODE 24, and it used to be wrong here. Only the KEY makes something a pattern: `{"./x": "./d/*.js"}` is not a pattern to Node, it loads the LITERAL path `d/*.js` and throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Expanding it produced N subpaths that all collapsed onto the one key `./x`, so the map kept whichever the file order put LAST — an arbitrary answer that would read as a change when an unrelated sibling file was added.

MEASURED: Node RESOLVES `{"./y/*": "./index.js"}` — every subpath in the family maps to that one file, so `pkg/y/anything` loads index.js. The pattern key is kept and its single target enumerated. Do NOT "fix" this to INDETERMINATE; that would red a package that works.

MEASURED: Node substitutes the capture into EVERY star, so a key `./z/*` over a two-star target resolves `pkg/z/sub` to `d/sub/sub.js`. Reverse-deriving the capture from a file path is then ambiguous — `d/sub/sub.js` yields capture `sub/sub`, which forward-substitutes to a DIFFERENT file — so this is INDETERMINATE rather than a glob that does not round-trip. The estate has no multi-star target; this keeps that measured.
69 of the estate's subpaths point at raw .ts source (the Astro shape). A compiler enumerates those exactly as it does a .d.ts.

files.src/index.ts:
export const web = 3
export type Web = typeof web

cases.why: A subpath with no `types` condition still has a name surface consumers import. allowJs makes it readable rather than indeterminate.

files.index.js:
export const web = 3
export function go() {}

cases.why: DETERMINABLY EMPTY, not unknown: the file parsed and declared nothing exportable. This is the third state that must not collapse into either of the other two.
No `exports` field: Level 2 never speaks for a legacy package, and the rule decides those pairs at Level 1.

THE DETERMINISM VECTOR. `localeCompare` orders these as a, B, Z, _x under en-US; codepoint order is B, Z, _x, a. A locale-sensitive sort makes the name set depend on the ICU locale of whichever machine ran the gate.
Names are identifiers, so line endings SHOULD not matter — asserted rather than assumed. Paired with ext-values-and-types-are-both-recorded, whose expectation must be byte-identical to this one.
A package with N subpaths over one .d.ts graph must answer identically per subpath — the shared-Program optimisation may not change any answer.

files.index.d.ts:
export * from "./inner.js";
export declare const top: number;

cases.why: The ordinary steady state: an entry written by a Level-2 engine carries the field and is served.

THE EMPTINESS TRAP (N1). An all-asset package is legitimately empty. Keying the guard off emptiness instead of FIELD PRESENCE would send those packages back to the registry on every run, forever, for no signal.

THE LOAD-BEARING GUARD. `{kind, subpaths}` and no names is what every entry written before Level 2 looks like. Accepting it hands the rule an empty reference name set, and a real named-export removal reads GREEN.
A null is not a names map. The test is a USABLE field, not a present key.
A2b over a malformed entry: the shape must be the one the rule indexes by subpath, or it proves nothing.
A legacy package still needs a v3-schema entry: a names-less one is stale, and staleness is decided by the schema, not by whether the rule happens to consult it.

The one exception, and it is fail-closed by construction: an unreadable surface never had names to carry, and `surfaceDelta` already returns required=null for it. Rejecting it would refetch forever to re-learn the same refusal.
No surface at all is the oldest entry shape of them all.
A2b over garbage: never throw, never accept.
